what_it_is: A stdlib-only Linux scheduler-side observation capture and report tool (scripts/observe_longrun.py) that can actually run for 7/30 days: fsync'd append-only JSONL samples (subject RSS/VmHWM/VmSize/threads/fd/uptime/alive plus host loadavg/MemAvailable/fs headroom), a manifest frozen at init binding workload/candidate/environment and *declared* windows, (boot_id, pid, starttime, comm) fingerprint segment records for subject restarts, and a report folding span/gap/sequence/torn-tail integrity with windows never exceeding the recorded span.
what_it_proves: 4 independent self-check scenarios pass via `python3 -I scripts/observe_longrun_test.py`: real-/proc sampling with honest window boundary (unobserved until span covers), window boundary inclusive edge, restart/absent/integrity surfaces (sequence gaps, torn tail bytes, manifest drift downgrading windows), and manifest immutability plus unresolved-PID honesty.
The tool appends durably and records sampler downtime as unobserved gaps rather than filling them.
what_it_does_not_prove: No 7-day or 30-day run has been performed or observed; no long-run data exists.
No RSS/drift/uptime/failure-distribution numbers for any Shenko candidate.
No router/Android/multi-node profiles, no power-loss RPO, no subject behavioural correctness (continuous thinking, no message loss) — the sampler observes process facts only.
Sampling is heartbeat-level: behaviour between samples and same-boot PID reuse without --pid-file supervision remain unobserved.

environment.executed_where: C19 worktree tooling only; self-test ran in the development container with local /proc

reproducer: python3 -I scripts/observe_longrun.py init --dir RUN_DIR --run-id ID --workload DESC --candidate-commit SHA --window 7d=604800 [--pid N|--pid-file F]
python3 -I scripts/observe_longrun.py sample --dir RUN_DIR   (cron/systemd) OR run --dir RUN_DIR --deadline-seconds N
